title: The whistle that isn't
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Gully, at the mill, says the whistle used to go at noon and you could hear it at the launch. Wood says he remembers. Gully says he wasn't asking. They stand there at noon. Nothing. The strip draws the nothing as a jagged shape that isn't there — a whistle's shape, empty, over the stack.

panels.composition: The mill yard, noon. GULLY looking up at the stack. WOOD. BARNABY.

balloons.text: Used to go at noon. Hear it at the launch.

image.prompt: a teenager and a young man standing in an overgrown mill yard at noon looking up at a brick stack, a small dog nearby, black and white, no words
close on the rim of a brick smokestack against a bright noon sky, nothing happening, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The stack, and over it, drawn as an empty outline: a jagged shape. A whistle's shape, with nothing in it.

image.prompt: a brick smokestack with a jagged empty outline drawn in the sky above it like the shape of a sound that isn't there, black and white, no words
image.notes: The whistle's jagged shape, empty. The canon draws it full in 2022 (ROFLCOPTER, The Mill 1994). Here: the outline only.

panels.composition: The two of them and the dog walking back to the fence. Noon past. Nobody heard anything. The strip drew the shape of it anyway.
